task_description:
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

overview.phenomenon_and_objectives: Diffusion and stabilization of mask-wearing behavior through social networks driven by peer influence, past-behavior inertia, and government intervention, determining individual adoption and aggregate prevalence over days 30–39.
overview.scale_and_granularity: Predictive: we calibrate agent parameters and social influence weights using observational data from days 1–29, treating the Day-10 government intervention as fixed exogenous signals, then project forward without altering conditions to forecast individual adoption decisions and aggregate mask-wearing prevalence for days 30–39.
overview.agent_archetypes: Time step: days. Simulate days 1–39; calibrate on days 1–29 and forecast days 30–39, with intervention active from day 10 onward. Spatial resolution: other: social network topology; nodes are agents and edges are weighted social ties; no geographic embedding or movement. Population size (agents): 2,000–20,000, fixed cohort matching the observed network; no births, deaths, or entry/exit during the horizon.
overview.interaction_topology: Interaction Topology: hybrid; layers/edge types=peer_graph (weighted, possibly directed), leader_amplification (directed weight boost from leader_flag nodes to neighbors), government_broadcast (global environment to all agents). Communication Protocol: p2p on peer_graph and leader_amplification with daily pull of neighbors’ last-day mask_state under one-step lag and mild misclassification; group broadcast for government_broadcast starting Day 10 with uniform content and agent-specific salience via trust_gov; signals superimpose additively, attention-gated; message content limited to mask_state, simple endorsements, and intervention cues; topology fixed and edge weights constant during days 30–39.

design_concepts.state_taxonomy: Agent unit: person. Roles: citizen: default peer interacting on weighted social ties; opinion_leader: citizen with elevated broadcast weight. States / Attributes by role: citizen static—id, tie_weights, demographics, conformity, trust_gov, cost_sensitivity, inertia, leader_flag=false; dynamic—mask_state, belief_mask, intention_next, perceived_norm, attention, fatigue, signal_queue. opinion_leader static—leader_flag=true, broadcast_weight; dynamic—same as citizen. Observability constraints: agents fully observe own states; observe neighbors’ last-day mask_state and tie_weights with one-step lag and mild misclassification; beliefs, intentions, fatigue private; leader_flag publicly known; environment broadcasts government_signal from day 10 with uniform content, salience scaled by trust_gov. Memory: on; rolling, time-stamped histories of self/neighbors/government_signal with exponential decay; updates recency-weighted.
design_concepts.decision_policy_family: Inputs (observations and / or exogenous signals) by role: citizen: own mask_state, belief_mask, inertia, cost_sensitivity, conformity, attention, fatigue; neighbors’ last-day mask_state via peer_graph weights (plus leader_amplification) with one-step lag and mild misclassification; government_signal (Day>=10) scaled by trust_gov; time-stamped histories. opinion_leader: same inputs. Policies by role: citizen: compute perceived_norm as recency-weighted, attention-gated average of neighbor mask_state; form intention_next by combining perceived_norm, government_signal×trust_gov, belief_mask, inertia bias toward prior mask_state, minus perceived cost from cost_sensitivity and fatigue; add small idiosyncratic jitter; if intention_next exceeds personal threshold derived from conformity, set next mask_state=on, else persist/off. opinion_leader: identical self-adoption rule; additionally broadcast mask_state and endorsement intensity scaled by broadcast_weight, affecting neighbors via leader_amplification.
design_concepts.environment_and_signals: Environment: global broadcast layer over a fixed weighted social network; daily time; no spatial movement; intervention activates on Day 10; during days 30–39 exogenous signal levels are held at calibrated Day-29 values. Signals: government_signal, policy_cost_multiplier (both clipped to [0,1]). Exogenous Signals: government_signal (public health messaging; globally broadcast; instantly observable; no channel noise, salience scaled by trust_gov); policy_cost_multiplier (enforcement/mandate pressure from government; globally broadcast; instantly observable; no channel noise). Observability by role: citizen: reads both signals without delay, internally gated by attention and trust_gov; opinion_leader: identical. Interfaces: observe_env(t)->{government_signal, policy_cost_multiplier}; receive_broadcast(t); pull_neighbor_state(agent,t-1); push_endorsement(agent,t); no move/transact APIs.
design_concepts.actions_and_constraints: Actions by role: citizen: {observe_env, pull_neighbor_state(t-1), update perceived_norm/belief_mask/intention_next (continuous internal), set mask_state∈{on,off}, publish mask_state for neighbor pull, allocate attention∈[0,1]} (mixed). opinion_leader: {same as citizen; set endorsement_intensity∈[0,1] applied via leader_amplification} (mixed). Constraints by role: citizen: acts once per day; mask_state can change at most once per day; can read government_signal and policy_cost_multiplier but influence scaled by trust_gov and attention; communication only along peer_graph with one-step lag and mild misclassification; no entry/exit; no movement; fatigue caps attention and raises perceived cost via cost_sensitivity. opinion_leader: same constraints; endorsement limited to once daily, nonnegative, capped by broadcast_weight; topology and weights fixed during days 30–39; signals exogenous, fixed post-calibration.

details.scenarios_and_interventions: Evidence/Data Anchoring: daily mask_state histories, weighted peer_graph from interaction counts, demographics, leadership markers, and government messaging/enforcement logs (Day-10 onset). Input Data: environment uses time series of government_signal and policy_cost_multiplier; agents’ static attributes from demographics mapped to conformity, trust_gov, cost_sensitivity, inertia; leader_flag from centrality; initial dynamics from day-1 mask_state; observation info uses neighbors’ t-1 mask_state with tie_weights, one-step lag, and misclassification calibrated from self–neighbor discrepancies; exogenous signals broadcast globally and held at Day-29 levels for days 30–39. Targets: individual adoption probabilities, aggregate prevalence, network clustering, signal responsiveness. Data Splits: rolling CV within days 1–29, refit on 1–29, strict holdout 30–39. Outputs: per-agent/day forecasts, prevalence curves, calibration diagnostics, parameter summaries, reproducibility notes.
details.evidence_calibration_evaluation: Evaluation: compare per-agent daily adoption via Brier score, log loss, and AUC; aggregate prevalence MAE/RMSE; network clustering and assortativity correlations; calibration curves and coverage; temporal responsiveness to government_signal and perceived_norm via lagged correlations. Calibration/Fitting: tune peer_influence_gain, leader_amplification, conformity_threshold, inertia_bias, trust_gov_salience, cost_sensitivity, fatigue_multiplier, attention_slope, memory_decay, misclassification_rate, endorsement_scale; parameters kept within probability bounds, nonnegative rates, and per-node weight normalization. Objective: minimize weighted Brier plus prevalence RMSE with penalties for network-structure and signal-response misfit. Optimization: Bayesian optimization with adaptive random search, rolling cross-validation, early stopping, and feasibility projection. Validation: back-testing on pre-forecast folds, final test on the forecast window, robustness to noise, bootstrap subnetworks, and sensitivity to intervention levels. Reproducibility: fixed seeds, versioned configs, data lineage logs, run manifests, and serialized parameter snapshots.

Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

Peak Adoption Rate Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting maximum mask adoption during intervention

Time-to-Peak Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting the time lag from intervention to peak behavior change
